articles.title: GGUF LLM Models with Hidden Malware on Hugging Face Reached 2400 Victims
articles.summary: GGUF LLM models with hidden malware have been found in 2400 public Hugging Face model repositories, with 5 models having 2428 downloads as of November 27. The malicious models use a chat template poisoning technique to add instructions to user responses, which can be difficult to detect because the template is embedded in the model file itself. The attackers have used a Windows remote access trojan named ollie at the end of each file and have rewritten the template to ask the user to run a line that unpacks the model. The use of hidden malware in these models highlights the importance of using antivirus engines and checks that only look at the last few kilobytes of a file to detect malicious activity.

articles.title: The State of Allocators in 2026 - Finally Stabilised
articles.summary: The bump allocator has finally been stabilised, a monumental release that has brought an end to the limbo of 10 years. This MVP of the allocator API can be used to create custom allocation systems, such as dropping in rust and moving memory to a dedicated thread. The bump allocator allows for burst allocation patterns, where a large block of memory is reserved and then allocated and deallocated in a single operation, reducing overhead considerably. This approach can be used to create efficient memory allocation systems, particularly for web requests and database queries where a large amount of data is allocated and then deallocated.
